newsitem.title: USA: Boeing, McDonnell Douglas unveil plan to merge.
newsitem.headline: Boeing, McDonnell Douglas unveil plan to merge.

text.p: The Boeing Co and McDonnell Douglas Corp announced on Sunday that they plan to merge, creating what industry sources said would be the largest aerospace company in the world.

The stock-for-stock merger, announced in a surprise news conference, will have huge implications for Airbus Industrie, the four-nation European consortium that is the other major player in the commercial aerospace industry.

Industry sources said the combined firm, to operate under the Boeing Co name, was projected to have 1997 sales of $47.7 billion, with about $28 billion from Boeing and $20 billion from McDonnell Douglas. Together, they would employ about 200,000 people and have a combined order backlog worth $100 billion.

Boeing chief executive Phil Condit told reporters he would serve as the combined company's chairman and chief executive, while McDonnell Douglas chief executive Harry Stonecipher would be its president and chief operating officer.

Boeing, based in Seattle, Washington, already has the leading position in the world commercial aircraft industry, historically holding a market share of about 50 percent and producing the 737, 747, 757, 767 and 777 airliners. It also has major defense activities, making such products as the F-22 fighter and the Chinook and Comanche military helicopters.

St. Louis, Missouri-based McDonnell Douglas is the third largest commercial aircraft company, and also makes a series of military aircraft, including the F/A-18 Hornet fighter, the C-17 Globemaster transport and the AH-64 Apache helicopter.
